actions.body:
Recent investigations into path dependence and preference formation reveal that sequential interactions and structured feedback loops, such as those seen in reinforcement learning from human feedback and multi-agent cultural transmission frameworks, enable artificial systems to develop consistent behavioral dispositions. By examining how historical interaction paths constrain future choices, we gain insight into the emergence of stable agent preferences.

Summary
This article explores how artificial intelligence systems can develop stable preferences through historical interaction and feedback, rather than relying exclusively on pre-programmed instructions.
